error_reason: The planner incorrectly deduced that mass changes when gravity changes, fundamentally confusing mass (invariant) with weight (proportional to gravity). This conceptual error at step 1 directly caused the selection of the wrong final answer (A instead of B), as no subsequent verification step could correct this foundational misunderstanding.

hypotheses.rationale: The planner incorrectly deduces that mass changes based on gravity, fundamentally misunderstanding the definition of mass versus weight. This error occurs before any verification step and directly causes the wrong final answer to be selected. Had the planner correctly verified that mass is invariant to gravity, they would have identified weight as the correct answer.
hypotheses.check: Verify that the agent checks the definition of mass (amount of matter, invariant) versus weight (force of gravity on mass, proportional to g) before concluding mass changes when gravity changes.

evidence.discrepancy: Step 1 claims that mass changes inversely with gravity ('Mass = weight ÷ gravity; with slightly lower gravity, mass would be the property perceived to change'). This contradicts the fundamental physical definition that mass is the amount of matter in an object and is invariant to changes in gravitational field strength. Consequently, the step incorrectly deduces that mass is less at the top of a mountain, whereas weight (mass × gravity) is the property that actually decreases.
